title: Cometary Globule CG4

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This picture from the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope shows CG4, a cometary globule. Cometary globules are isolated clouds of gas and dust in our galaxy. They get their name because their shape can resemble a comet's head and tail, although they have nothing to do with comets.

The telescope's Mosaic II camera recorded CG4 through four filters. Three let through blue, green and near-infrared light. The fourth isolates one particular shade of red, called hydrogen-alpha, which warm hydrogen gas gives off.

Pairing broad filters with a narrow one is a common approach in astronomical imaging. The broad filters record the general colours of stars and dust, while the hydrogen-alpha filter shows where glowing hydrogen is found. The near-infrared filter reaches just beyond the red end of what the eye can see.

understand.summary: The Blanco 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic II camera observed CG4 through blue, green, near-infrared and hydrogen-alpha filters. The colours assigned to each filter in the final picture are not published.
